elements.element: Vendor duty to indemnify Customer and its affiliates
elements.evidence: "indemnify Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses"

elements.element: Coverage: data breach caused by Vendor

"(iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct"
"Company shall give Contractor prompt written notice of any such claim"

elements.element: Standard procedure: Vendor control of defence
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall have control of the defense"

elements.element: Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: No Customer indemnity exists anywhere in Section 7 or the inserted text; condition demonstrably absent, so no limitation is required.
"(i) an allegation that the Services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"
Inserted 7(d) contains no exclusions; no reference to modifications, combinations or Specifications.
No remedy ladder appears; text ends with the limitations carve-out.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3x annual fees
elements.evidence: "are not subject to the limitations set forth in Sections 7(a), 7(b) and 7(c)" — uncapped, no 3x figure.

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are present in operative language: defend and indemnify, Customer plus affiliates, and all four coverage triggers (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct).
Procedure is limited to the three permitted mechanics (notice, control, cooperation); no hold-harmless, no Customer defence duty, no added indemnitees, no settlement-consent mechanics.
The conditional Customer-indemnity limitation is satisfied because no Customer indemnity exists in the clause or document; none was invented.

The insertion is a concise new subsection for an absent clause; the carve-out from Sections 7(a)-(c) is necessary to avoid a dangling contradiction with the existing fees-paid cap and the mutual attorneys'-fees waiver, and does not rewrite the untouched liability provisions.

Fallback is not met (no usual exclusions, no procure/modify/replace/refund ladder, no 3x annual fees super-cap), but the locked target is preferred and the two levels are not combined; the available super-cap is correctly offered only in the non-operative comment.
Unrelated commercial terms in 7(a)-(c) remain effective and no undefined term is introduced ("Services", "Confidential Information" and "Statement of Work" are defined in the Agreement).
